title: [Advisory] Microsoft Patch Tuesday November 2026
content:
##### SEVERITY AND IMPACT:
**Current exploitation status:** 
- Actively Exploited: (CVE-2026-124194 Microsoft Outlook Spoofing Vulnerability)
- Publicly Disclosed: None

##### NOTABLE CVEs:
- **CVE-2026-116928** CVSS3.1: 9.8 (CRITICAL) - Windows Search RCE. Pre-auth RCE on Exchange server via malicious attachment automatically processed by Exchange/Windows Search. Assume SYSTEM; patches are for Windows OS, affecting Exchange Subscription Edition.
- **CVE-2026-119952** CVSS3.1: 8.1 (HIGH) - Windows Schannel RCE. Pre-auth RCE via specially crafted packets against the TLS implementation. Specific conditions are required, but exploitation is assessed as more likely; possible SYSTEM depending on service.
- **CVE-2026-124194** CVSS3.1: 6.5 (MEDIUM) - Microsoft Outlook Spoofing (Actively Exploited). Opening a malicious file causes Outlook to connect to an attacker-controlled location and leak the user’s NTLMv2 hash. The hash can be relayed live or cracked offline; Preview Pane is not a vector. Patches cover classic Outlook and affected Microsoft 365 Apps for Enterprise / Office installations.

##### REFERENCES:
Primary:
- Source Advisory: https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/releaseNote/2026-Nov

Supporting:
- Additional Sources: https://www.rapid7.com/blog/post/patch-tuesday-november-2026-em
- Additional Sources https://www.securityweek.com/exploited-outlook-zero-day-among-1094-flaws-patched-by-microsoft/

*Timestamp of the Information: 11.11.2026, 12:10*
summary: Microsoft’s November 2026 Patch Tuesday addresses over 1,000 vulnerabilities across its portfolio, including multiple critical pre-authentication remote code execution flaws and one actively exploited Outlook zero-day. The most urgent issues affect Windows Schannel, Windows Search/Exchange integration, and Outlook NTLMv2 hash disclosure. No other vulnerabilities in this release were publicly disclosed or known to be exploited.
